headline: Light showers brush the north Tuesday, warm dry weather Thursday and Friday, then rain and breezy winds return Sunday into Monday.
summary: Monday night is quiet. High clouds are moving in, which should limit fog and frost, though patchy valley fog and some frost are still possible. Lows should be in the upper 30s to mid 40s. A weather system passing through British Columbia will just clip western Washington Tuesday into early Wednesday. Light showers are expected mainly along the Pacific coast, on the western Olympic slopes, and from King County northward. Amounts should be small: a few hundredths of an inch in the northern inland areas and a quarter to half an inch on the North Coast. High pressure aloft rebuilds Wednesday and showers fade through the day. Thursday and Friday should be warm, with highs in the mid 60s to mid 70s, because winds near the ground blow from land toward the coast rather than off the ocean. Friday is the warmest day, about 5 to 10 degrees above normal. A weak, fading system brings some rain Saturday, mainly to the coast and North Cascades. A stronger system Sunday into Monday brings more widespread rain and breezy winds, with highs only in the upper 50s to mid 60s. Snow levels may drop to 5000-5500 feet Monday, so a dusting on the higher peaks is possible. Forecasters are confident in the midweek warm spell, since models strongly agree that high pressure builds Thursday. Weekend timing and amounts are less certain.
changes: The morning discussion expected highs up to the lower 70s Thursday and a Friday peak in the mid 70s, with Friday over 10 degrees above normal. Later discussions lowered that to 5 to 10 degrees above normal and added more detail on the Sunday-Monday rain and wind. The morning Frost Advisory expired with no new hazards.
